Smoother game streaming on Windows when your GPU is busy. Nexo updates itself: look for the
**Restart to update** banner.

## What's new

- **Fast game capture (Windows).** Nexo now keeps captured frames on the GPU instead of copying every
  frame back to the CPU. A heavy game that keeps the GPU near 100% used to drop streams to ~8–30 fps. With
  this change the stream keeps up with the game (in testing, ~30 → ~55 fps). It's on by default. You can
  turn it off in **Settings → App → Fast game capture** (takes effect after restarting Nexo) if your stream
  ever shows a black or frozen picture.
  - On Windows older than **11 24H2**, it only applies when you share a **window**. Share the game's
    window instead of the entire screen.
- **Clearer low-fps hint.** When the capture is starved, the hint now explains how to give the GPU some
  headroom (graphics settings, upscaling, and an FPS cap *below* what the game reaches).

Your stream still can't be smoother than your game. An **uncapped** game still starves the capture, so
cap it.

## Install

Already on v0.2.0-alpha.1 or later? Nothing to do: Nexo updates itself.

New here? Download the file for your system from the **Assets** below. The installers are **not
code-signed**, so your OS will warn you the first time.

- **Windows:** run `Nexo-Setup-<version>.exe`. If SmartScreen says "Windows protected your PC", click
  **More info → Run anyway**.
- **macOS:** open the `.dmg` and drag Nexo to **Applications**. The first time, **right-click Nexo →
  Open → Open**. If macOS says the app "is damaged", run `xattr -cr /Applications/Nexo.app` in Terminal.
- **Linux:** `chmod +x Nexo-*.AppImage && ./Nexo-*.AppImage`.

No server changes: hosts don't need to update anything.
